name: Hoham
overview: Hoham was a male king who ruled over the city of Hebron during the time of the Israelite conquest of the Promised Land. His reign is noted specifically in the biblical account of Joshua, identifying him as a regional ruler opposing Israel's advance. Beyond his kingship of Hebron, Scripture does not provide further tribal or familial details about him.
namesAndTitles: The name 'Hoham' appears as a proper name without a given meaning in the biblical text. He is also identified by the title 'King of Hebron,' which straightforwardly denotes his political authority over that city during the conquest period, as recorded in Joshua 10:3.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Hoham beyond his role as king of Hebron. No additional relatives or tribal affiliations are mentioned in the biblical account.
scriptureSignificance: Hoham's significance lies in his position as a local king resisting Israel's divinely ordained conquest of the land. His mention in Joshua 10:3 places him among the coalition of kings opposing Joshua and the Israelites, highlighting the political and military challenges faced during this critical period in redemptive history. Though briefly noted, his role reflects the broader narrative of God's judgment and promise fulfillment through Israel's conquest.
